title: Choose the visual world
question: The app should feel like Catwees and Honda. This is the direction to build. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Workshop job card
options.lineage: The paper work order clipped to a Honda at the Catwees hoist
options.thesis: Every screen is a field on the work order that follows your Honda.
options.viewport: A phone-sized sheet: Honda and Catwees in the header, a red stamp, the plate number as the largest type, notices as ruled lines, one action at the foot.
options.risk: It turns bureaucratic if the plate and the stamp are set timidly.

raised.raise: A fore-edge of four sections. Only the current tab extends.
Red marks only the live edge of the active field. It never floods the sheet.
Guest and signed-in are two phases of the same sheet: blank, then stamped with name and plate.
Mileage, time, and year are measured readouts with a unit.
Four states only: empty, filled, error, sent.

options.label: Catwees reception
options.lineage: The red bar and white sheet of catwees.ee, carried onto the phone
options.thesis: The owner recognizes the Catwees desk before reading a word.
options.viewport: Red bar with both logos, a car photograph, then stacked notice rows and a bottom menu.
options.risk: This is the familiar dealer-app look. Most runs in this category land here, and it can slide back into a marketing homepage.

options.label: Red decision bands
options.lineage: Airport overhead signs, recoloured to Catwees red
options.thesis: Each screen asks only the next decision, with the plate number at gate scale.
options.viewport: Stacked red bands for service, a claim, and a test drive. The registration number sits below them like a gate number, with the next open slot.
options.case: Clearer on a phone, one decision at a time. Weaker identification: the owner's scene is the Catwees desk, not a concourse.
options.risk: It feels like transit signage if the bands multiply past the one next step.

options.label: Owner's manual
options.lineage: A tabbed Honda handbook with a coloured divider board
options.thesis: The app is the owner's manual, and booking is a leaf in the service section.
options.viewport: A fore-edge of coloured tabs, the open section filling the page.
options.case: Owners know the book, but a binder is a poor booking form.
options.kept: Only the current section tab extends, and its size shows how much of the relationship it holds.
options.risk: Section colours fight the red-and-charcoal brand.

options.label: Cloud edge
options.lineage: A white cloud with a narrow spectral fringe
options.thesis: The page stays white, and only a coloured edge marks what is active.
options.viewport: Wide empty margins and a thin coloured fringe on the active notice.
options.case: The fringe is useful. The pastel cloud is not a Honda owner's scene, and it hides the form.
options.kept: Colour stays on the live edge. The reading field stays achromatic.
options.risk: Pastel edges read as weather, not as a dealer.

options.label: Cyclorama
options.lineage: A theatre cyc washing from night to day
options.thesis: Signing in is a lighting cue: the same sheet goes from blank to occupied.
options.viewport: A full-bleed dawn behind the owner's name.
options.case: A phase change is right. Cobalt and rose are not Catwees, and they bury the task.
options.kept: Guest and signed-in are named phases of one sheet, not a small avatar swap.

options.label: Oscilloscope
options.lineage: A phosphor trace on a service-bench scope
options.thesis: The car's numbers are instrument readouts on a dark graticule.
options.viewport: One dark screen, mileage and time as glowing readouts.
options.case: Measured numbers belong. A dark instrument bench is not how an owner books a loan car in daylight.
options.kept: Mileage, time, and year are measured against a scale and always carry a unit.
options.risk: Green-on-black reads as a diagnostic toy.

options.label: Arcade screen
options.lineage: A pixel-art cabinet with a strict sixteen-colour law
options.thesis: Every state is a sprite swap inside a fixed palette.
options.viewport: A tiled playfield with the plate as a score.
options.case: A four-state palette law is worth keeping. An arcade cabinet is the wrong room for a claim.
options.kept: Four ink states only: empty, filled, error, sent.
options.risk: Playfulness undercuts a damage claim and a trade-in.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A normal owner app: top bar, photo, white cards, red button, bottom tabs.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a dealer app usually ships, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other service app by design.
